items.title: Precision fixes for website discovery: zero wrong answers on both scored benchmarks
items.body:
## What this is

Four defects found and fixed in the discovery classifier, plus a corrected benchmark ground truth. On the two datasets that can be scored, the tool now writes **no wrong answers at all** — every remaining error is a miss.

| Dataset | Rows | Answers written | Wrong | Review leads | Nothing | Precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 227 human-verified | 227 | 213 | **0** | 11 | 3 | **100%** |
| Agri-IoT | 62 | 31 | **0** | 11 | 20 | **100%** |
| Space-Tech FAIL | 59 | 13 | — | 27 | 19 | no verified column |
| 100-company sample | 100 | 26 | — | 26 | 48 | no labels |

227 Category A is **198 of 199**, and the one miss isn't wrong — iAeroSky returned the correct URL, just held as a review lead.

## The fixes

**1. `browser-only-reachable` fired on domains that resolve for nobody.** A DNS lookup now runs alongside the browser probe and the plain fetch. A host with no A/AAAA record that still renders a `200` is a monetised NXDOMAIN wildcard — `3spacecorp.com` returns `200` and redirects to `parklogicchannel.com`. Measured: **40 of the 41** rows carrying this reason had no DNS record. It was roughly half the human review worklist.

**2. A parked verdict came from a single DNS resolution.** `iaerosky.com` publishes two A records — one serves Hostinger's parking page, one serves the real site. Round-robin made every probe a coin flip, and a parked verdict was terminal. Each address is now asked separately before the domain is called dead.

**3. A junk lead permanently suppressed the platform-host stage.** `tryPlatformHosts` was gated on having nothing better than a `review` lead, so any medium lead — a holding page, an intercepted dead domain — blocked the one stage that can find a vercel/netlify-hosted site. Gate removed; `noteLow` now breaks ties by evidence specificity; the stage picks the *best* brand-matching platform host rather than the first.

**4. Domains listed for sale, detected by nameserver.** `klonec.com` sits on Afternic and serves a different response per request — empty on `www`, a redirect on the apex, sometimes enough text to pass a content match, which is how it was written in as an answer. The page flickers; the NS record does not.

**5. A site-builder banner was rejecting real sites.** "Go from idea to live site in minutes / Get 50 free credits" was an unconditional placeholder marker. `dilekaaerospace.com` has 2,583 characters of genuine company copy under that strip and was being thrown away.

## Ground truth is now a file, not the spreadsheet

`website-agent-diagnostics/ground-truth-overrides.json` is authoritative. 12 sheet labels were verified wrong — 9 rows marked PASS are holding pages (`stardour.com` renders 89 characters, `husori.com` renders 10) or dead domains (`orbitx.in` is parked, `spacebelief.co.in` returns a Wix 404). Scoring against them was charging the tool for being right. Applied idempotently from a `.orig` snapshot; the client sheet is never modified.

Two entries are owner calls that direct URL checks contradict — **Prakshep** and **SmartGro**, whose sheet URLs are both live, substantial, on-topic sites. Applied as instructed, with the contradicting evidence recorded beside each entry so the 100% figure stays auditable.

## Two things reviewers should know

**A rule was withdrawn, not shipped.** A stage-1 content bar was built on the claim that `raudranexaerospace.in` serves a titleless `200`. It actually serves a GoDaddy lander and was already handled correctly; the observed failure was environmental flapping. The attempt broke three legitimate tests and was reverted rather than weakened to fit.

**A fix was corrected mid-review.** `namebrightdns.com` was initially treated as a for-sale nameserver. `cosmicport.com` sits on it and serves a real site, so it was removed — the empty NameBright domains are already caught by the structural placeholder rule. Only true marketplaces qualify now.

## Also in this PR

- `input/production/…xlsx` (4.6 MB of real company records) removed from tracking, and `input/**/*.xlsx|xls|csv` gitignored. **This does not remove it from git history** — that needs a rewrite, which is not done here.
- `architecture.md` rewritten: its folder tree, per-company flow and layer table all referenced a `steps/` directory and five files that no longer exist.
- README gains a command reference at the top and a three-command first-run sequence.
- `engineering.md` gains "Evidence over assumption", recording the rules on this branch that were written from theory and turned out wrong on real pages.

169 tests pass; typecheck clean.

items.title: Verify engine correctness in a downstream job that reuses benchmark results
items.body:
## Summary

Second of two PRs for #126. #127 committed the ground-truth answers; this PR adds the **correctness check** that verifies every participating engine returns them, and **fails CI on a mismatch**.

Rather than a separate workflow that re-executes all 60 (engine × query) runs a second time, it **reuses the benchmark's runs**. The benchmark already runs every `(engine, query, scale factor)`, so it now also *dumps* each result, and a **downstream `verify-correctness` job — which `needs` the benchmark jobs — compares those dumps to the committed answers** in a clean, engine-free step. No duplicated execution; the comparison happens where no engine is installed, so none of the SedonaDB/pyarrow import-order pitfalls apply.

## What changed

**`run_benchmark.py`** — new `--result-dir`. After a query's timed runs, it captures the result (new `result_dataframe()` hook), normalizes it (durations → seconds, decimals → float, timestamps → datetime), and writes `<engine>_<query>_result.csv`. Runs in the same isolated-subprocess pattern and writes **csv only** (never parquet), so no pyarrow filesystem is touched inside a SedonaDB worker; pandas/numpy stay out of the module top to preserve the import-order isolation. Gated on committed answers existing for the scale factor, so **SF10 (no answers yet) does no extra work**.

**`benchmark/verify_results.py`** (new, engine-free) — compares each dumped result to its committed answer csv and renders a per-engine correctness table to the job summary:
- **By column position** (engines name the same column differently, e.g. `avg_duration` vs `avg_duration_seconds`).
- Integer keys / strings / timestamps exact; floats with `rtol=1e-6`, `atol=1e-9`; a within-tolerance **`LIMIT`-boundary-row** difference passes.
- **Exits non-zero on any mismatch → fails CI.** An engine that could not compute a query (timeout / error / OOM, e.g. DuckDB's lateral-join Q12 at scale) is reported (⏱️) but does **not** fail the job — that's a runtime issue, surfaced by the benchmark summary, not a wrong answer.

**`benchmark.yml`** — engine jobs pass `--result-dir` and upload the result csv alongside the timing json (pandas added to the Spatial Polars / PyCanopy jobs, whose dumps convert polars → pandas). New **`verify-correctness`** job: `needs` the benchmark jobs, downloads their results, runs `verify_results.py`, publishes the correctness table to the job summary, and fails on a mismatch.

## Example summary (published to the job)

| Query | 🦆 DuckDB | 🐼 GeoPandas | 🌵 SedonaDB | 🐻‍❄️ Spatial Polars | 🌴 PyCanopy |
|:------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Q1** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Q12** | ⏱️ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

✅ matches · ❌ mismatch (fails CI) · ⏱️ couldn't compute (not a failure) · — not verified.

## Local validation (SF1)

- SedonaDB / DuckDB / GeoPandas result dumps → all **✅** against the committed answers, including timestamp queries (Q3/Q5) and Q4's ~260-row result.
- Corrupting a dumped value → the table shows **❌** with a precise per-column/row detail and `verify_results.py` **exits 1** (CI would fail).
- SF10 (no committed answers) → no result dumps, verify job exits 0 with a "not checked" note.

Spatial Polars and PyCanopy use the identical dump path and are exercised by CI.

## Notes

- Answers exist for **SF1** only, so verification is active at SF1; **SF10** answers + verification to follow.
- The generator that produced the answers stays uncommitted (per review on #127); the verify job only reads the committed answers.

items.title: perf(splat): Triton tile kernels (tiling="triton") — 15.8× over the tiled path at G=10k
items.body:
Executes [docs/plans/2026-07-06-triton-tile-kernel-plan.md](../blob/main/docs/plans/2026-07-06-triton-tile-kernel-plan.md) task-by-task (subagent-driven: fresh implementer per task, per-task spec+quality review, one fix wave, final whole-branch review). 7 commits.

## What

`splat_render_cubics(..., tiling="triton", tile_size=16)` — Triton forward+backward tile kernels (CUDA + float32 only; informative errors elsewhere; `tiling="auto"` still resolves to `"tiles"`). New module `pydiffvg/splat_triton.py`: segment builder (sorted per-(batch,tile) gaussian lists), forward kernel with a register-resident per-pixel log-transmittance accumulator (one store per pixel, **no atomics in forward** — deterministic per tile, an improvement over the scatter-add tiles path), hand-derived backward kernel with per-gaussian atomic grad accumulation, autograd.Function wrapping only the accumulator (1−exp/crop/clamp stay in PyTorch autograd). Composes with `pixel_box`, batching, and the zero-pair graph stub. The gray-wash cutoff (`mahal_sq < 20`, strict) is replicated exactly and was verified per-review against both PyTorch references.

## Measured (RTX 5090, idle — verified 0 compute procs; torch 2.10.0+cu128, Triton 3.6.0, fp32, fwd+bwd)

| config | tiled ts=16 | **triton** | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 384², G=10,240 | 47.05 ms | **2.98 ms** | **15.8×** (acceptance bar ≥5× — PASSED) |
| 768², G=10,240 | 136.5 ms | **3.96 ms** | **34.5×** |
| 384², G=40,960 | ~182 ms | ~7 ms | ~26× |
| peak memory @ G=10,240 | 728 MB | **33 MB** | 22× less |

Span across the sweep: 1.65× (G=96) to 34.5×. Against the original dense renderer, scene-scale rendering has gone 728 ms → 2.98 ms (244×) across the three merged stages. Benchmark: `CPATH=... uv run python benchmarks/bench_splat_tiling.py --device cuda` (triton arm added; exactness-gated before timing, all gates ≤4.8e-7).

## Exactness evidence

- `tests/test_splat_triton.py` (12 tests): segment-builder unit tests; direct-kernel accum parity vs the tiles path; gradient parity via `autograd.grad` (worst measured **2.3e-10** vs the 1e-5 gate); end-to-end forward+grad vs dense at both tile sizes; pixel_box composition; zero-pair white/zero-grads; CUDA/fp32/tile_size validation. Full suite: **188 passed, 2 pre-existing CPU skips**.
- Adversarial sweep: `adversarial gate OK` — border-straddling fwd 2.98e-7/grad 3.7e-9; hairline σ=1e-2 fwd 1.25e-6/grad 1.18e-6; zero-opacity fwd 3.6e-7/grad 7e-9.
- **Default-path byte-identity** vs origin/main: forward AND gradients `torch.equal` on CPU+CUDA across 3 configs, re-verified after the final fix wave — `BYTE-IDENTICAL`.

## One plan amendment (human-approved mid-execution)

The plan's adversarial near-zero-σ gate (σ=1e-6, grad ≤1e-5 absolute) is unattainable for any op-order-independent fp32 kernel: FMA contraction in `dc` amplified by ~1e8 inverse variance flips pixels across the hard cutoff (each flip ≈ exp(−10)·opacity). Task 4 correctly BLOCKED on this; the approved amendment splits the case — σ=1e-2 at the full ≤1e-5 gates (passes at 1.3e-7), σ=1e-6 at forward ≤1e-5 + finite-grads (committed regression test documents the rationale; plan doc updated in-branch). No kernel math was altered; the wiring and kernels remain byte-identical to the spike-validated plan code.

Per-task reviews all Approved (Task 3's reviewer independently re-derived every gradient line; Task 4's verified sanctioned-lines-only byte-level; Task 5's caught a README figure citing the wrong benchmark column — fixed).
